lessons.title: Using ChatGPT and Claude

cards.title: What an AI assistant is
lines: ChatGPT and Claude are AI assistants.
You type or speak. They answer in text.
They are built on large language models.

cards.title: What they do well
lines: Explain ideas in simple words.
Summarise long text.
Draft emails and reports.
Make lists and checklists.
Turn rough notes into clear writing.

cards.title: What they do not do well
lines: Know your exact relay and firmware.
Do exact calculations without a check.
Remember things you did not tell them.
Be right every time.

cards.title: A fast new assistant
lines: Imagine a new assistant who reads fast and writes well.
He has never seen your site or your relay.
You give clear instructions.
You check his work.

cards.title: Your first good chat
lines: Say who you are and what you need.
Give the background in two or three lines.
Say how you want the answer.
Ask follow-up questions.

cards.title: Example chat
lines: Prompt: Explain overcurrent protection to a new technician in 5 short lines. Use a simple example.
Then check the answer against a trusted textbook or manual.
Ask a follow-up: Now explain pickup and time delay in simple words.

cards.title: Free and paid versions
lines: Both tools have free versions with limits.
Features and limits change often.
Check each tool's own page to see what is free today.

cards.title: Before you type
lines: Do not type company secrets, customer names or private settings.
Remove names and numbers you are not allowed to share.
The next lesson covers this fully.

cards.title: Practice: ask and check
lines: Ask an AI to explain what trip circuit supervision does, in simple words.
Compare the answer with a manual or textbook.
Write one correct point and one point you need to check.

cards.title: Recap
lines: AI assistants explain, summarise and draft well.
They do not know your relay. Give context and check the result.
Never type confidential data.

quiz.q: Which task are AI assistants usually good at?
quiz.why: They are strong with language tasks such as summaries and drafts.

quiz.q: What does the 'fast new assistant' comparison tell you?
options: Give clear instructions and check the work
quiz.why: AI is capable but new to your situation, so guide it and verify.

options: Who you are, what you need and the format you want
quiz.why: Context and format lead to better answers.

quiz.q: What should you do with an AI's explanation of a protection function?
options: Use it as an approved procedure
Check it against a trusted manual or textbook
quiz.why: AI explanations are a starting point and must be verified.

quiz.q: Which is safe to type into a public AI tool?
options: General question: how does overcurrent protection work?
quiz.why: General learning questions are fine. Do not share confidential data.

lessons.career: Using an AI assistant well, with context and checking, is already a useful workplace skill.

lessons.title: Hallucinations, Privacy and Confidential Data

cards.title: Hallucinations again
lines: An AI can state false things with confidence.
It may invent a standard number, a setting or a source.
It does not know that it is wrong.

cards.title: A realistic danger
lines: It might quote a setting range that does not exist for your relay.
It might name an IEC clause that is wrong.
A wrong number in a test plan can cause real problems.

cards.title: How to catch mistakes
lines: Ask: where does this come from?
Check every number in the manual.
Ask the same question in another way and compare.
Be extra careful with numbers, names and dates.

cards.title: Match your care to the risk
lines: The riskier the task, the more you must check.

cards.title: Privacy: where your text goes
lines: Many tools may keep what you type.
Some may use chats to improve their systems, depending on the tool and your settings.
Read the privacy settings before you use any tool for work.

cards.title: What counts as confidential
lines: Customer names and site details.
Internal test reports and drawings.
Real relay settings files.
Company software, passwords and keys.

cards.title: Safer habits
lines: Remove names and numbers before you ask.
Practise with made-up (synthetic) data.
Ask your company which AI tools are approved.
Use approved tools for work files.

cards.title: Your rule
lines: If you are not sure it is allowed, do not paste it.
Ask your manager or IT team first.
AI output is a draft. An engineer approves.

cards.title: Practice: clean a risky prompt
lines: Risky: Summarise the settings of Relay R1 at Customer X's Plant Y.
Rewrite it with no real names or numbers.
Example: Explain in general what an overcurrent relay setting sheet usually contains.

cards.title: Recap
lines: AI can be confidently wrong, so check numbers and sources.
Higher risk needs more checking.
Never paste confidential data. Ask first.

options: A confident answer that is wrong or invented
quiz.why: Hallucinations sound sure but are false.

quiz.q: Which task needs the MOST checking?
quiz.why: Limits, settings and safety steps are high risk.

quiz.q: What is a safe way to practise with AI?
If you are unsure whether you may paste something, you should...
options: Not paste it and ask first
quiz.why: When in doubt, do not paste it. Ask your manager or IT team.

options: A general definition of a relay
quiz.why: Internal reports and customer details are confidential.

lessons.career: Engineers who check AI output and protect data are trusted with AI tools. Careless users are not.

lessons.title: Writing Structured Prompts

cards.title: Why structure helps
lines: A vague question gets a vague answer.
A clear prompt saves time.
Four parts work well: goal, context, format and boundaries.

cards.title: Goal
lines: What do you want?
Example: Make a pre-test checklist.

cards.title: Context
lines: Who is it for, and what is the background?
Example: For a new technician. General secondary injection test.

cards.title: Format
lines: How should the answer look?
Example: A table with three columns and no more than 10 rows.

cards.title: Boundaries
lines: What should the AI avoid or limit?
Example: Do not give setting values. Say 'check the approved procedure' where a limit is needed. Use simple English.

cards.title: Weak and strong prompts
lines: See the difference side by side.

head: Weak prompt
Strong prompt
rows: Explain what a protection relay does to a new technician in 5 lines, with one simple example
Make a pre-test checklist for a general overcurrent relay. Table: Step, What to check, Tick box. No setting values
Review this test sheet layout for missing fields. List problems as bullets. Do not rewrite it

cards.title: A full example
lines: Goal: Make a pre-test checklist for a general overcurrent relay secondary injection test.
Context: For a new technician. This is a fictional training example, no real site.
Format: A table with Step, What to check and Tick box.
Boundaries: Do not give setting values. Add 'check approved procedure' where a limit is needed.

cards.title: Improve, do not restart
lines: If the answer is not right, say what to change.
Examples: shorter, simpler, add a table.
Ask the AI to list what it is unsure about.

cards.title: A checklist from AI is a draft
lines: Compare it with your company's approved test procedure before use.
Add missing steps yourself.
The engineer is responsible, not the AI.

cards.title: Practice: write a four-part prompt
lines: Write a prompt that asks an AI to explain CT saturation simply.
Include goal, context, format and boundaries.
Run it, then check the answer against a textbook.

cards.title: Recap
lines: Goal, context, format, boundaries.
Improve by giving feedback, not by starting again.
Check AI drafts against approved documents.

quiz.q: What are the four parts of a structured prompt in this lesson?
quiz.why: Goal, context, format and boundaries make prompts clear.

options: Explain relays to a new technician in 5 lines with one example
quiz.why: The strong prompt gives audience, length and format.

options: Something the AI should avoid or limit
quiz.why: For example: do not give setting values.

quiz.q: The AI's first answer is not quite right. What next?
A checklist written by AI should be...
quiz.why: AI drafts must be checked against approved documents.

lessons.career: Clear structured prompts save time and reduce mistakes in reports, checklists and learning.
